cards.definition: **Definition.** The output change divided by input change over a nonzero interval, equal to the corresponding secant slope.
major_error_concepts: Dividing output change by an absolute final input value instead of the nonzero input difference.
cards.prompt: Define Average rate of change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The output change divided by input change over a nonzero interval, equal to the corresponding secant slope.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The secant-slope expression [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h for h nonzero whose limit may define f'(a).
major_error_concepts: Substituting h=0 before cancelling the factor h.
cards.prompt: Define Difference quotient. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The secant-slope expression [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h for h nonzero whose limit may define f'(a).

cards.definition: **Definition.** A rule assigning each allowed input exactly one output while preserving the declared domain, codomain, and image.
major_error_concepts: Treating a displayed formula as defined for every real number.
cards.prompt: Define Function as a mapping. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A rule assigning each allowed input exactly one output while preserving the declared domain, codomain, and image.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The mapping x -> f(g(x)) with a domain requiring x in dom(g) and g(x) in dom(f).
major_error_concepts: Intersecting the written domains without checking that g(x) lands in dom(f).
cards.prompt: Define Function composition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The mapping x -> f(g(x)) with a domain requiring x in dom(g) and g(x) in dom(f).

cards.definition: **Definition.** For a function f:A to B, the domain is the declared input set A; it may be a strict subset of the natural domain on which a displayed formula is defined.
major_error_concepts: Checking only the logarithm or only the square root.
cards.prompt: Define Function domain. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The domain of f:A to B is the declared input set A.
A formula's natural domain can be larger than the declared domain.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of outputs actually attained from the declared domain rather than the stated codomain.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the image consists only of endpoint outputs without analyzing values attained in the interior of the declared domain.
cards.prompt: Define Function image. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of outputs actually attained from the declared domain rather than the stated codomain.

cards.definition: **Definition.** substitution into the complete defining rule with parentheses and domain checks preserved.
major_error_concepts: Replacing x by a+h in only one occurrence.
cards.prompt: Define Function notation and evaluation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: substitution into the complete defining rule with parentheses and domain checks preserved.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The controlled horizontal or vertical shift, scale, or reflection of a base graph.
major_error_concepts: Calling the transformation y=f(x-c) a left shift of the base graph when c>0 under the usual horizontal-translation convention.
cards.prompt: Define Function transformation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The controlled horizontal or vertical shift, scale, or reflection of a base graph.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The equivalence between an input-output pair f(a)=b and the graph point (a,b).
major_error_concepts: Swapping input and output when converting f(a)=b into its graph point (a,b).
cards.prompt: Define Graph-function correspondence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The equivalence between an input-output pair f(a)=b and the graph point (a,b).

cards.definition: **Definition.** A piecewise-defined function uses different formulas on declared subsets of its domain, with each input assigned according to the condition attached to the applicable formula.
major_error_concepts: Using a formula at a boundary point without checking whether its condition includes that point.
cards.prompt: Define piecewise-defined function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A piecewise-defined function uses different formulas on declared subsets of its domain.
Each input is assigned according to the condition attached to the applicable formula.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The variable meaning, admissible values, and dimensional unit that constrain algebraic calculus operations.
major_error_concepts: Dropping units and later adding quantities with incompatible dimensions.
cards.prompt: Define quantity and units.
required_concepts: The variable meaning, admissible values, and dimensional unit that constrain algebraic calculus operations.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inverse obtained only after restricting a non-one-to-one rule to an interval where each output has one input.
major_error_concepts: Writing plus-or-minus sqrt(y) as a function inverse.
cards.prompt: Define Restricted inverse function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inverse obtained only after restricting a non-one-to-one rule to an interval where each output has one input.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The conjunction that f(a) is defined, lim x->a f(x) exists, and that limit equals f(a).
major_error_concepts: Checking only that f(1) is defined.
cards.prompt: Define Continuity at a point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The conjunction that f(a) is defined, lim x->a f(x) exists, and that limit equals f(a).

cards.definition: **Definition.** Common point discontinuities include removable, jump, infinite or unbounded, and oscillatory behavior; the list is a practical classification rather than an exhaustive taxonomy in arbitrary spaces.
major_error_concepts: Calling every missing point a vertical asymptote.
cards.prompt: Define Common elementary discontinuity types. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Includes removable and jump discontinuities.
Includes infinite or unbounded and oscillatory discontinuities.
The list is qualified rather than universally exhaustive.

cards.definition: **Definition.** for every positive output tolerance epsilon there exists a positive input tolerance delta making 0<abs(x-a)<delta imply abs(f(x)-L)<epsilon.
major_error_concepts: Choosing epsilon after seeing x, which reverses the quantifier order.
cards.prompt: Define epsilon-delta definition of a limit.
required_concepts: for every positive output tolerance epsilon there exists a positive input tolerance delta making 0<abs(x-a)<delta imply abs(f(x)-L)<epsilon.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It guarantees that a continuous objective on a closed bounded interval has actual global extrema, so an optimization argument may search for values rather than merely an unattained supremum or infimum; it gives neither the locations nor uniqueness of those extrema.
major_error_concepts: Using boundedness of the written endpoint values as a substitute for a closed interval.
cards.prompt: What is Extreme Value Theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It guarantees that a continuous objective on a closed bounded interval has actual global extrema, so an optimization argument may search for values rather than merely an unattained supremum or infimum
it gives neither the locations nor uniqueness of those extrema.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** A continuous real function on a closed bounded interval attains both an absolute maximum and minimum.
major_error_concepts: Using boundedness of the written endpoint values as a substitute for a closed interval.
cards.prompt: State Extreme Value Theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: The function is real-valued and continuous on a closed bounded interval [a,b].
The function attains an absolute maximum at some point of [a,b].
The function attains an absolute minimum at some point of [a,b].

cards.definition: **Definition.** The single finite value approached by f(x) as x approaches a from both sides, independent of f(a).
major_error_concepts: Substituting first, obtaining 0/0, and calling 0/0 the limit.
cards.prompt: Define Finite two-sided function limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The single finite value approached by f(x) as x approaches a from both sides, independent of f(a).

cards.definition: **Definition.** unbounded magnitude with a declared sign as x approaches a, describing behavior rather than a real output value.
major_error_concepts: Writing f(0)=infinity.
cards.prompt: Define Infinite function limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: unbounded magnitude with a declared sign as x approaches a, describing behavior rather than a real output value.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It proves existence of an input attaining an intermediate output, most often a root after an endpoint sign change; it does not locate the input or prove that it is unique.
major_error_concepts: Claiming uniqueness from IVT alone.
cards.prompt: What is Intermediate Value Theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It proves existence of an input attaining an intermediate output, most often a root after an endpoint sign change
it does not locate the input or prove that it is unique.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** A continuous function on [a,b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b).
major_error_concepts: Claiming uniqueness from IVT alone.
cards.prompt: State Intermediate Value Theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: The function f is continuous on the closed interval [a,b].
For every value L between f(a) and f(b), there is a point c in [a,b] such that f(c)=L.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The limiting behavior of f(x) as the input grows without bound, used to identify long-run levels or divergence.
major_error_concepts: Substituting infinity as though it were a real number.
cards.prompt: Define Limit at infinity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The limiting behavior of f(x) as the input grows without bound, used to identify long-run levels or divergence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The algebra of limits applied only when component limits exist and quotient denominators have nonzero limiting value.
major_error_concepts: Applying the quotient law when the denominator limit is zero.
cards.prompt: Define limit laws and hypotheses.
required_concepts: The algebra of limits applied only when component limits exist and quotient denominators have nonzero limiting value.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The value approached under the additional restriction x<a or x>a.
major_error_concepts: Equating a point value f(a) with one-sided limits without establishing the appropriate one-sided limiting behavior or continuity.
cards.prompt: Define One-sided function limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The value approached under the additional restriction x<a or x>a.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It transfers a limit from two simpler bounding functions to a trapped target whose direct limit is difficult to evaluate; both bounds must apply near the point and converge to the same value.
major_error_concepts: Concluding a target limit merely from boundedness, without lower and upper bounds that apply near the point and converge to the same value.
cards.prompt: What is Squeeze theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It transfers a limit from two simpler bounding functions to a trapped target whose direct limit is difficult to evaluate
both bounds must apply near the point and converge to the same value.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If g(x)<=f(x)<=h(x) for all x sufficiently near a, possibly excluding a, and lim g(x)=lim h(x)=L as x approaches a, then lim f(x)=L.
major_error_concepts: Concluding a target limit merely from boundedness, without lower and upper bounds that apply near the point and converge to the same value.
cards.prompt: State Squeeze theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: The eventual inequalities g(x)<=f(x)<=h(x) hold in a punctured neighborhood of a.
The lower and upper functions have the same limit L as x approaches a.
The trapped function f has limit L as x approaches a.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The conclusion that no common finite or extended value satisfies both directions, with an explicit separating mechanism.
major_error_concepts: Averaging distinct one-sided limits and reporting that average as the two-sided limit.
cards.prompt: Define Two-sided limit nonexistence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The conclusion that no common finite or extended value satisfies both directions, with an explicit separating mechanism.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The limit of the difference quotient giving instantaneous output change per input change at one point.
major_error_concepts: Substituting h=0 before simplifying the quotient.
cards.prompt: Define Derivative at a point. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The limit of the difference quotient giving instantaneous output change per input change at one point.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The function assigning each input where it exists the derivative computed from a moving difference quotient.
major_error_concepts: Computing only f'(a) at one point and calling it the derivative function.
cards.prompt: Define Derivative function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The function assigning each input where it exists the derivative computed from a moving difference quotient.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** The theorem licenses continuity at a point from a finite derivative there, but it cannot be reversed to infer differentiability from continuity.
major_error_concepts: Using continuity alone to claim that a derivative exists.
cards.prompt: What is Differentiability implies continuity used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: A finite derivative supplies continuity at the same point.
The converse fails, for example at a cusp.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If f is differentiable at a, then f is continuous at a; continuity at a need not imply differentiability there.
major_error_concepts: Assuming continuity guarantees differentiability.
cards.prompt: State the differentiability-implies-continuity theorem at a point, including its hypothesis, conclusion, and nonconverse.
required_concepts: Differentiability of f at a implies continuity of f at a.
Continuity at a does not imply differentiability at a.

cards.definition: For real x, d(e^x)/dx=e^x and d(a^x)/dx=a^x ln(a) for a>0. For x>0, d(ln x)/dx=1/x and d(log_a x)/dx=1/(x ln a), where a>0 and a is not 1. More generally d(ln|x|)/dx=1/x for x not zero.
major_error_concepts: The derivative of 2^x is 2^x, and the derivative of log_2 x is 1/x.
cards.prompt: State the derivatives of e^x, a^x, ln x, and log_a x, with their real-domain restrictions.
required_concepts: The derivatives of e^x and a^x are e^x and a^x ln a.
The derivatives of ln x and log_a x are 1/x and 1/(x ln a).
State the positive-argument and valid-base restrictions for real logarithms.

cards.definition: For the standard principal branches, (arcsin x)'=1/sqrt(1-x^2) and (arccos x)'=-1/sqrt(1-x^2) for |x|<1; (arctan x)'=1/(1+x^2) for every real x. Arcsin and arccos are defined at ±1 but do not have finite ordinary derivatives there.
major_error_concepts: The derivatives of arcsin and arccos are both 1/sqrt(1-x^2), including at x=1.
cards.prompt: State the principal-branch derivatives of arcsin x, arccos x, and arctan x, including where the formulas apply.
required_concepts: Arcsine has derivative 1/sqrt(1-x^2) for |x|<1.
Arccosine has the negative of that derivative on the same interval.
Arctangent has derivative 1/(1+x^2) on the real line.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A corner, cusp, vertical tangent, discontinuity, or oscillatory quotient that prevents a finite common derivative.
major_error_concepts: Calling every nondifferentiable point a discontinuity.
cards.prompt: Define Nondifferentiability mechanism. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A corner, cusp, vertical tangent, discontinuity, or oscillatory quotient that prevents a finite common derivative.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A difference-quotient limit restricted to increments from one side, needed at domain boundaries or corners.
major_error_concepts: Averaging unequal left and right difference-quotient limits to manufacture an ordinary two-sided derivative.
cards.prompt: Define One-sided derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A difference-quotient limit restricted to increments from one side, needed at domain boundaries or corners.

cards.definition: The derivative of a constant is zero. For a constant exponent p, d(x^p)/dx=p x^(p-1) wherever the real power is differentiable (in particular x>0 for arbitrary real p). If f and g are differentiable and a,b are constants, (af+bg)'=af'+bg'. Polynomial powers with nonnegative integer p extend to all real x with their usual derivatives.
major_error_concepts: The derivative of x^p is x^(p-1), and the derivative of a nonzero constant is that constant.
cards.prompt: State the constant, power, and linearity rules for differentiation and note the power rule's domain restriction.
required_concepts: A constant differentiates to zero.
The power rule is p x^(p-1) on a valid differentiability domain.
Differentiation preserves constant linear combinations.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative identity (fg)'=f'g+fg' rather than the product of derivatives.
major_error_concepts: Replacing (fg)' by f'g', or systematically omitting one nonzero term from f'g+fg'.
cards.prompt: Define Product rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The derivative identity (fg)'=f'g+fg' rather than the product of derivatives.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative identity (f/g)'=(f'g-fg')/g^2 at points where g is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Using denominator g rather than g squared or losing the subtraction order.
cards.prompt: Define Quotient rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The derivative identity (f/g)'=(f'g-fg')/g^2 at points where g is nonzero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative of a scalar one-variable composition as the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function times the inner derivative.
major_error_concepts: Claiming (f composed with g)' equals f'(g(x)) for arbitrary differentiable g without the inner derivative factor g'(x).
cards.prompt: Define Scalar single-variable chain rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The derivative of a scalar one-variable composition as the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function times the inner derivative.

cards.definition: With angles in radians: (sin x)'=cos x, (cos x)'=-sin x, (tan x)'=sec^2 x, (cot x)'=-csc^2 x, (sec x)'=sec x tan x, and (csc x)'=-csc x cot x. Each formula applies where the original function is defined; other angle units require the chain-rule conversion factor.
major_error_concepts: With degree input, the derivative of cos x is sin x and tan x is differentiable where cos x=0.
cards.prompt: State the six basic trigonometric derivatives for radian input and their domain convention.
required_concepts: Give the six stated radian-based derivatives with their correct signs.
Exclude zeros of any denominator in the original function.
The standard formulas assume radian input.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The magnitude of estimate minus truth and that magnitude scaled by a declared nonzero reference.
major_error_concepts: Reporting signed error as absolute error or dividing by the approximation without declaring that convention.
cards.prompt: Define Absolute and relative approximation error. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The magnitude of estimate minus truth and that magnitude scaled by a declared nonzero reference.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The first-order change dy=f'(x)dx used to estimate a small output change while retaining its local character.
major_error_concepts: Calling dy the exact finite change without comparison to Delta y.
cards.prompt: Define Differential estimate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The first-order change dy=f'(x)dx used to estimate a small output change while retaining its local character.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The model y'=ky with solution behavior characterized by the signed proportional rate k.
major_error_concepts: Inferring a continuous proportional rate k from a multiplicative change alone without its elapsed time and the exponential-law relation.
cards.prompt: Define Exponential growth-decay rate law. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The model y'=ky with solution behavior characterized by the signed proportional rate k.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The derivative obtained by differentiating a relation while treating the dependent variable as a function and checking the point and denominator.
major_error_concepts: Using a point that fails the defining relation, or dividing by a solved-for derivative coefficient that is actually zero at the point.
cards.prompt: Define Implicit derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The derivative obtained by differentiating a relation while treating the dependent variable as a function and checking the point and denominator.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local reciprocal derivative formula (f^{-1})'(b)=1/f'(a) when b=f(a) and f'(a) is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Evaluating the reciprocal derivative at the inverse input b instead of the corresponding preimage a=f^{-1}(b), without checking that distinction.
cards.prompt: Define Inverse-function derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local reciprocal derivative formula (f^{-1})'(b)=1/f'(a) when b=f(a) and f'(a) is nonzero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The tangent-line approximation L(x)=f(a)+f'(a)(x-a) intended near a.
major_error_concepts: Treating the tangent-line approximation as an exact identity for an arbitrary nonlinear function away from the base point.
cards.prompt: Define Linearization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The tangent-line approximation L(x)=f(a)+f'(a)(x-a) intended near a.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The neighborhood and regularity evidence limiting how far a tangent or differential approximation may be trusted.
major_error_concepts: Assuming an affine formula derived locally inherits the original function's global validity.
cards.prompt: Define Local-validity boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The neighborhood and regularity evidence limiting how far a tangent or differential approximation may be trusted.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The method of taking logarithms to turn variable powers or products into differentiable sums under valid sign/domain conditions.
major_error_concepts: Taking ln of a nonpositive expression without a domain argument.
cards.prompt: Define Logarithmic differentiation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The method of taking logarithms to turn variable powers or products into differentiable sums under valid sign/domain conditions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** successive time derivatives connecting position, velocity, and acceleration with signed units.
major_error_concepts: Calling speed and velocity identical when velocity can be negative.
cards.prompt: Define Position velocity acceleration chain. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: successive time derivatives connecting position, velocity, and acceleration with signed units.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An equation among time-dependent quantities differentiated before inserting an instant's measurements.
major_error_concepts: Replacing a time-varying quantity by its instantaneous numeric value before differentiation and incorrectly erasing its time derivative.
cards.prompt: Define Related-rates dependency model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An equation among time-dependent quantities differentiated before inserting an instant's measurements.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The affine function using a point and derivative to match value and first-order change locally.
major_error_concepts: Using the function value f(a) as the tangent slope in place of the derivative f prime(a), without justification that they coincide in the particular case.
cards.prompt: Define Tangent-line model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The affine function using a point and derivative to match value and first-order change locally.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A vertical, horizontal, or slant line supported by the corresponding one-sided or infinite limiting behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling every denominator zero a vertical asymptote without checking cancellation.
cards.prompt: Define asymptotes and limiting behavior.
required_concepts: A vertical, horizontal, or slant line supported by the corresponding one-sided or infinite limiting behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** evaluation of all interior critical candidates and both endpoints to identify absolute extrema on a closed interval.
major_error_concepts: Checking only derivative-zero points and omitting endpoints.
cards.prompt: Define Closed-interval extrema method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: evaluation of all interior critical candidates and both endpoints to identify absolute extrema on a closed interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The upward or downward bending inferred from the sign of f'' on intervals where it exists.
major_error_concepts: Calling f''(0)=0 an interval of zero concavity.
cards.prompt: Define Concavity from second derivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The upward or downward bending inferred from the sign of f'' on intervals where it exists.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interior domain point where f'=0 or f' does not exist, serving as a candidate rather than proof of an extremum.
major_error_concepts: Discarding points where f' is undefined even though f is defined.
cards.prompt: Define Critical number. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interior domain point where f'=0 or f' does not exist, serving as a candidate rather than proof of an extremum.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inference that a positive derivative gives increase and a negative derivative gives decrease on an interval.
major_error_concepts: Testing signs only at the critical points where the derivative is zero.
cards.prompt: Define Derivative-sign monotonicity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inference that a positive derivative gives increase and a negative derivative gives decrease on an interval.

cards.definition: Let f be continuous at c and differentiable on both sides near c. A change of f' from positive to negative gives a strict local maximum at c; a change from negative to positive gives a strict local minimum. If f' keeps one strict sign across c, c is not a local extremum. A zero derivative alone is inconclusive.
major_error_concepts: A positive-to-negative derivative sign change gives a local minimum even if f is discontinuous at c.
cards.prompt: State the first-derivative sign test for local maxima and minima, including the condition at the candidate point.
required_concepts: Positive-to-negative derivative gives a local maximum.
Negative-to-positive derivative gives a local minimum.
Require continuity at the candidate and the stated signs on nearby intervals.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A domain point across which concavity changes, not merely a zero or undefined second derivative.
major_error_concepts: Using f''(0)=0 as sufficient proof.
cards.prompt: Define Inflection-point evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A domain point across which concavity changes, not merely a zero or undefined second derivative.

cards.definition: For a one-sided limit x→a, let f and g be differentiable on a punctured one-sided interval, with g(x) and g'(x) nonzero there. Suppose f/g has the indeterminate form 0/0 or infinity/infinity, and lim f'(x)/g'(x)=L exists as a finite or extended real value. Then lim f(x)/g(x)=L. The corresponding two-sided conclusion requires the same conclusion from both sides; analogous tail statements hold at infinity. The rule is sufficient, not necessary.
major_error_concepts: Differentiate numerator and denominator to replace any quotient limit, even when the original form is 1/0.
cards.prompt: State a sufficient one-sided version of L'Hopital's rule, including the indeterminate form and regularity hypotheses.
required_concepts: Require differentiability and a nonzero denominator derivative on the relevant punctured interval.
Require a 0/0 or infinity/infinity indeterminate form.
The derivative quotient must have a limit L; then the original quotient has that limit.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It converts endpoint-average change into an attained instantaneous rate, supporting monotonicity, error, and comparison arguments; it requires its continuity and differentiability hypotheses and does not identify a unique interior point.
major_error_concepts: Claiming MVT identifies a unique c in every function.
cards.prompt: What is Mean Value Theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It converts endpoint-average change into an attained instantaneous rate, supporting monotonicity, error, and comparison arguments
it requires its continuity and differentiability hypotheses and does not identify a unique interior point.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** The equality f'(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a) at some interior c under closed-interval continuity and open-interval differentiability.
major_error_concepts: Claiming MVT identifies a unique c in every function.
cards.prompt: State Mean Value Theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: The function f is continuous on the closed interval [a,b].
The function f is differentiable on the open interval (a,b).
There is a point c in (a,b) such that f'(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a).

cards.definition: **Definition.** The tangent-based update x_{n+1}=x_n-f(x_n)/f'(x_n) with domain, derivative, stopping, and failure checks.
major_error_concepts: Reporting an iterate as a certified root without residual or error evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Newton iteration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The tangent-based update x_{n+1}=x_n-f(x_n)/f'(x_n) with domain, derivative, stopping, and failure checks.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The objective, constraints, feasible domain, units, boundary cases, and decision criterion established before differentiation.
major_error_concepts: Differentiating two unconstrained variables without using the perimeter constraint.
cards.prompt: Define optimization problem formulation.
required_concepts: The objective, constraints, feasible domain, units, boundary cases, and decision criterion established before differentiation.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It detects at least one interior stationary point when a differentiable curve returns to the same endpoint value and serves as the equal-endpoint case behind the Mean Value Theorem; it does not locate or make that point unique.
major_error_concepts: Using an endpoint as the guaranteed interior point.
cards.prompt: What is Rolle theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It detects at least one interior stationary point when a differentiable curve returns to the same endpoint value and serves as the equal-endpoint case behind the Mean Value Theorem
it does not locate or make that point unique.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** The guarantee of an interior horizontal tangent for a function continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and equal at the endpoints.
major_error_concepts: Using an endpoint as the guaranteed interior point.
cards.prompt: State Rolle theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: Continuity on [a,b], differentiability on (a,b), and equal endpoint values are the hypotheses.
Those hypotheses guarantee an interior point c in (a,b) with f'(c)=0.

cards.definition: If f is twice differentiable near c and f'(c)=0, then f''(c)>0 gives a strict local minimum and f''(c)<0 gives a strict local maximum. If f''(c)=0, this test is inconclusive: a minimum, maximum, or neither can occur.
major_error_concepts: At a stationary point a positive second derivative gives a maximum, and zero proves there is no extremum.
cards.prompt: State the second-derivative test at a stationary point, including the zero case.
required_concepts: Require a stationary point f'(c)=0 and the stated differentiability.
Positive second derivative means minimum; negative means maximum.
Zero second derivative is inconclusive.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The unique limiting signed accumulation represented by Riemann sums when that limit exists independently of admissible sample choices.
major_error_concepts: Treating the integral symbol as requiring an antiderivative before it has been defined.
cards.prompt: Define Definite integral. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The unique limiting signed accumulation represented by Riemann sums when that limit exists independently of admissible sample choices.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A sufficient bounded-interval condition such as continuity or piecewise continuity that licenses the Riemann integral in this course.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every unbounded function on an open interval has an ordinary Riemann integral.
cards.prompt: Define First-course integrability criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A sufficient bounded-interval condition such as continuity or piecewise continuity that licenses the Riemann integral in this course.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The sum of f(x_i*) Delta x_i over a partition, interpreted through a limit as mesh tends to zero.
major_error_concepts: Dropping unequal subinterval widths.
cards.prompt: Define General Riemann sum. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The sum of f(x_i*) Delta x_i over a partition, interpreted through a limit as mesh tends to zero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The identity integral_a^c f plus integral_c^b f equals integral_a^b f under compatible integrability.
major_error_concepts: Replacing signed subinterval integrals by their magnitudes when applying integral additivity.
cards.prompt: Define Integral additivity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The identity integral_a^c f plus integral_c^b f equals integral_a^b f under compatible integrability.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The constant height f_avg=(1/(b-a)) integral_a^b f giving the same signed accumulation on a nonzero interval.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by b rather than b-a.
cards.prompt: Define Integral average value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The constant height f_avg=(1/(b-a)) integral_a^b f giving the same signed accumulation on a nonzero interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The consequence m<=f<=M on [a,b] implies m(b-a)<=integral f<=M(b-a) for a<b.
major_error_concepts: Treating an inequality bound as an exact integral value without equality conditions; a valid loose bound is not itself an error.
cards.prompt: Define Integral comparison bound. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The consequence m<=f<=M on [a,b] implies m(b-a)<=integral f<=M(b-a) for a<b.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The preservation of scalar multiplication and addition by the definite-integral operator.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying bounds by the coefficients.
cards.prompt: Define Integral linearity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The preservation of scalar multiplication and addition by the definite-integral operator.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The convention reversing bounds negates the integral and identical bounds give zero.
major_error_concepts: Treating reversed bounds as absolute area.
cards.prompt: Define Integral orientation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The convention reversing bounds negates the integral and identical bounds give zero.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The cancellation or doubling rules for odd or even integrands on symmetric intervals.
major_error_concepts: Applying the odd rule on a nonsymmetric interval.
cards.prompt: Define Integral symmetry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The cancellation or doubling rules for odd or even integrands on symmetric intervals.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An ordered finite subdivision a=x0<x1<...<xn=b used to organize local contributions.
major_error_concepts: Listing four points and thereby creating only three subintervals.
cards.prompt: Define Interval partition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An ordered finite subdivision a=x0<x1<...<xn=b used to organize local contributions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** rectangular accumulation using left or right subinterval endpoints with widths retained.
major_error_concepts: Averaging endpoint heights before declaring a left or right sum.
cards.prompt: Define Left and right Riemann sums. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: rectangular accumulation using left or right subinterval endpoints with widths retained.

cards.definition: **Definition.** rectangular accumulation using each subinterval midpoint as the sample point.
major_error_concepts: Using the midpoint of the whole interval for both rectangles.
cards.prompt: Define Midpoint Riemann sum. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: rectangular accumulation using each subinterval midpoint as the sample point.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The largest subinterval width, whose approach to zero expresses uniform refinement control.
major_error_concepts: Using the average width instead of the largest width.
cards.prompt: Define Partition mesh. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The largest subinterval width, whose approach to zero expresses uniform refinement control.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared choice of one point in each subinterval at which the integrand is sampled.
major_error_concepts: Selecting subinterval left endpoints while claiming to apply its right-endpoint sample-point rule, or sampling outside the assigned subinterval.
cards.prompt: Define Sample-point rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The declared choice of one point in each subinterval at which the integrand is sampled.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The compressed representation of an indexed finite sum with explicit start, end, and summand.
major_error_concepts: Omitting the index bounds and leaving the number of terms ambiguous.
cards.prompt: Define Sigma notation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The compressed representation of an indexed finite sum with explicit start, end, and summand.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral's positive-above and negative-below contributions versus the nonnegative area obtained by absolute value or sign splitting.
major_error_concepts: Calling cancellation zero evidence that no geometric region exists.
cards.prompt: Distinguish Signed accumulation versus geometric area.
required_concepts: Signed accumulation integrates f, so contributions above the axis are positive and contributions below the axis are negative.
Geometric area is nonnegative and is obtained by integrating abs(f) or by splitting at sign changes.
Signed accumulation permits cancellation between opposite signs, whereas geometric area does not.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The variable-upper-bound function A(x)=integral_a^x f(t)dt recording net accumulation from a fixed base.
major_error_concepts: Confusing dummy integration variable t with upper-limit variable x during differentiation.
cards.prompt: Define Accumulation function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The variable-upper-bound function A(x)=integral_a^x f(t)dt recording net accumulation from a fixed base.

cards.definition: **Definition.** all antiderivatives on an interval differing by an arbitrary constant.
major_error_concepts: Omitting C in an indefinite-integration result.
cards.prompt: Define Antiderivative family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: all antiderivatives on an interval differing by an arbitrary constant.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A function F satisfying F'=f on a declared interval.
major_error_concepts: Checking by integrating again rather than differentiating F.
cards.prompt: Define Antiderivative. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A function F satisfying F'=f on a declared interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A change of variable in which both integrand/differential and limits are converted to the new variable.
major_error_concepts: Using u-bounds and then substituting x into the antiderivative.
cards.prompt: Define Definite substitution with bounds. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A change of variable in which both integrand/differential and limits are converted to the new variable.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of signed velocity versus the integral of speed or a sign-split sum.
major_error_concepts: Taking the absolute value of total displacement and calling it total distance.
cards.prompt: Distinguish Displacement versus total distance.
required_concepts: Displacement is the signed net change given by the integral of velocity.
Total distance is the nonnegative accumulation given by the integral of speed abs(v), equivalently by sign splitting.
Opposite-direction motion cancels in displacement but still contributes positively to total distance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** for continuous f, the accumulation function A(x)=integral_a^x f(t)dt satisfies A'(x)=f(x).
major_error_concepts: Evaluating the integral first and then forgetting the theorem's continuity setting.
cards.prompt: Define FTC Part I. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: for continuous f, the accumulation function A(x)=integral_a^x f(t)dt satisfies A'(x)=f(x).

cards.definition: **Definition.** for continuous f with antiderivative F, integral_a^b f=F(b)-F(a).
major_error_concepts: Computing F(a)-F(b).
cards.prompt: Define FTC Part II evaluation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: for continuous f with antiderivative F, integral_a^b f=F(b)-F(a).

cards.definition: **Definition.** The reverse-chain-rule change of variable that transforms integrand and differential consistently.
major_error_concepts: Changing x^2 to u but leaving dx unchanged.
cards.prompt: Define Indefinite substitution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The reverse-chain-rule change of variable that transforms integrand and differential consistently.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The use of one condition to select a unique member of an antiderivative family.
major_error_concepts: Substituting the initial condition into y' instead of y.
cards.prompt: Define Initial-value constant selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The use of one condition to select a unique member of an antiderivative family.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The independent check that a proposed antiderivative differentiates to the original integrand on the stated domain.
major_error_concepts: Writing ln x as the only real antiderivative on negative x.
cards.prompt: Define Integration verification by differentiation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The independent check that a proposed antiderivative differentiates to the original integrand on the stated domain.

cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It converts an accumulated rate over an interval into the signed change of an antiderivative, linking definite integrals to physical change; it does not by itself give total variation, final amount, or a rate-valued answer.
major_error_concepts: Reporting 6 liters/hour after integrating over time.
cards.prompt: What is Net Change Theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
required_concepts: It converts an accumulated rate over an interval into the signed change of an antiderivative, linking definite integrals to physical change
it does not by itself give total variation, final amount, or a rate-valued answer.

cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If F is differentiable on [a,b] and F' is integrable there, for example continuous, then integral_a^b F'(x) dx=F(b)-F(a).
major_error_concepts: Reporting 6 liters/hour after integrating over time.
cards.prompt: State Net Change Theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
required_concepts: F is differentiable on [a,b] and F' is integrable there.
The integral of F' from a to b equals F(b)-F(a).

cards.definition: If f is continuous on the relevant integration region and u,v are differentiable, then d/dx integral from u(x) to v(x) of f(t) dt = f(v(x))v'(x)-f(u(x))u'(x). The lower-endpoint contribution is subtracted. This formula assumes the integrand depends on t, not also explicitly on x.
major_error_concepts: Always add both endpoint contributions and ignore any explicit x dependence of the integrand.
cards.prompt: State the derivative of an integral with two moving endpoints and an integrand f(t) independent of x.
required_concepts: Use f(v(x))v'(x) minus f(u(x))u'(x).
Require a continuous integrand and differentiable endpoints.
This version has no explicit x dependence in the integrand.

cards.definition: If f is continuous near g(x), g is differentiable, and H(x)=integral from a to g(x) of f(t) dt is defined, then H'(x)=f(g(x))g'(x). Evaluate the integrand at the moving endpoint and multiply by that endpoint's derivative.
major_error_concepts: The derivative of integral from a to g(x) of f(t) dt is f(x), regardless of g.
cards.prompt: State the FTC chain rule for H(x)=integral from a to g(x) of f(t) dt.
required_concepts: Evaluate f at the moving endpoint g(x).
Multiply by g'(x).
Require continuity of f and differentiability of g at the relevant points.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The constant function value producing the same total accumulation over the interval.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the arithmetic mean of endpoint values always equals the integral average, without conditions or a direct verification that justifies that equality.
cards.prompt: Define Application average-value model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The constant function value producing the same total accumulation over the interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An independent bound, sign, unit, limiting-case, symmetry, or coarse numerical check on an evaluated calculus model.
major_error_concepts: Accepting exact symbolic algebra without comparing the result to geometric bounds.
cards.prompt: Define Application sanity check. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An independent bound, sign, unit, limiting-case, symmetry, or coarse numerical check on an evaluated calculus model.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of upper-minus-lower or right-minus-left after intersections and sign order determine the bounds.
major_error_concepts: Reporting negative geometric area by integrating lower minus upper, or retaining a fixed ordering across crossings without splitting or taking the appropriate absolute difference.
cards.prompt: Define Area-between-curves model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The integral of upper-minus-lower or right-minus-left after intersections and sign order determine the bounds.

cards.definition: **Definition.** volume accumulation 2pi(radius)(height)(thickness) for slices parallel to the rotation axis.
major_error_concepts: Using diameter 2x as the radius and multiplying by 2pi again.
cards.prompt: Define Cylindrical-shell volume method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: volume accumulation 2pi(radius)(height)(thickness) for slices parallel to the rotation axis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** volume accumulation pi R(x)^2 dx when slices perpendicular to an axis are solid disks.
major_error_concepts: Using radius x but forgetting to square it.
cards.prompt: Define Disk volume method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: volume accumulation pi R(x)^2 dx when slices perpendicular to an axis are solid disks.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A geometric accumulation using thickness dy and a cross-section described as right minus left or an area function of y.
major_error_concepts: Using top-minus-bottom with dy.
cards.prompt: Define Horizontal-slice model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A geometric accumulation using thickness dy and a cross-section described as right minus left or an area function of y.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The choice among signed accumulation, area, slicing, disks/washers, shells, work, mass, or average value from the modeled differential element.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a named formula before fixing axis, slice direction, radius, and height.
cards.prompt: Define Integration-method selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The choice among signed accumulation, area, slicing, disks/washers, shells, work, mass, or average value from the modeled differential element.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of linear density over position with density units multiplied by length units.
major_error_concepts: Averaging endpoint densities without justification for a nonlinear density.
cards.prompt: Define Mass-from-density model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The integral of linear density over position with density units multiplied by length units.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integral of force over displacement after expressing the force law and coordinate consistently.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying final force ka by distance a and ignoring variation.
cards.prompt: Define Variable-force work model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The integral of force over displacement after expressing the force law and coordinate consistently.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A geometric accumulation using thickness dx and a cross-section described as top minus bottom or an area function of x.
major_error_concepts: Writing right-minus-left while still integrating in x.
cards.prompt: Define Vertical-slice model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A geometric accumulation using thickness dx and a cross-section described as top minus bottom or an area function of x.

cards.definition: **Definition.** volume accumulation pi[R^2-r^2] dx or dy for cross-sections with an inner radius.
major_error_concepts: Using pi(R-r)^2 instead of pi(R^2-r^2).
cards.prompt: Define Washer volume method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: volume accumulation pi[R^2-r^2] dx or dy for cross-sections with an inner radius.

deck.description: Learn limits, continuity, derivatives, applications of differentiation, definite integrals, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
deck.subject: Mathematics
deck.title: Calculus I
